p = pathlib.Path("src/dataq/plugins/builtin/features.py"); s = p.read_text()
s = s.replace('''def _time_column(profile) -> str | None:
    times = profile.by_role("time")
    return times[0].name if times else None''',
'''def _time_column(profile, named: str | None = None) -> str | None:
    """The column to order events by, checked for being usable as one.

    A named column is verified rather than trusted: a text column that *means* a
    timestamp fails as `VARCHAR - INTERVAL` deep inside DuckDB, and that error
    names a type mismatch rather than the column or the fix.
    """
    if named:
        column = profile.column(named)
        if column is None:
            raise ValueError(f"no column named {named!r}")
        if not is_temporal(column.physical_type):
            raise ValueError(_not_temporal(column))
        return named
    times = profile.by_role("time")
    return times[0].name if times else None


def _not_temporal(column) -> str:
    """Why a column cannot be a time axis, and what to do about it."""
    detail = (f"{column.name} is {column.physical_type}, not a date or timestamp, "
              "so it cannot be used as a time axis.")
    if SEMANTIC_TYPES.matches_any(column.semantic_type, ("temporal",)):
        formats = next((g.formats for g in column.candidates if g.formats), [])
        how = f" (it reads as {formats[0].label})" if formats else ""
        detail += (f" It does hold dates{how} -- parse it first with "
                   "normalize.timestamp, which will add a real timestamp column.")
    return detail''')
s = s.replace('''from ...core import features as F
from ...query.spec import QuerySpec, Select, Sort, TimeBucket''',
'''from ...core import features as F
from ...core.profile import is_temporal
from ...core.semantic import SEMANTIC_TYPES
from ...query.spec import QuerySpec, Select, Sort, TimeBucket''')
s = s.replace("        time_column = p.time_column or _time_column(ctx.profile)\n"
              "        if (p.grain or p.windows) and not time_column:",
              "        time_column = _time_column(ctx.profile, p.time_column)\n"
              "        if (p.grain or p.windows) and not time_column:")
s = s.replace("        time_column = p.time_column or _time_column(ctx.profile)\n\n"
              "        join = self._join(ctx, p, known) if p.from_dataset else None",
              "        time_column = _time_column(ctx.profile, p.time_column)\n\n"
              "        join = self._join(ctx, p, known) if p.from_dataset else None")
s = s.replace("            time_column = p.time_column or _time_column(ctx.profile)\n"
              "            if not time_column:",
              "            time_column = _time_column(ctx.profile, p.time_column)\n"
              "            if not time_column:")
p.write_text(s)

# The pre-existing time rollup fails the same way; the user hit it too.
p = pathlib.Path("src/dataq/plugins/builtin/aggregators.py"); s = p.read_text()
s = s.replace('''    def plan(self, ctx: AggregateCtx) -> AggregatePlan:
        p: TimeRollupParams = ctx.params
        select = [Select(column="*", agg="count", alias="n")]''',
'''    def plan(self, ctx: AggregateCtx) -> AggregatePlan:
        p: TimeRollupParams = ctx.params
        column = ctx.profile.column(p.time_column)
        if column is None:
            raise ValueError(f"no column named {p.time_column!r}")
        if not is_temporal(column.physical_type):
            # date_trunc and strftime both reject VARCHAR, and the binder error
            # they raise names neither the column nor the remedy.
            raise ValueError(
                f"{p.time_column} is {column.physical_type}, not a date or "
                "timestamp. If it holds dates as text, parse it first with "
                "normalize.timestamp."
            )
        select = [Select(column="*", agg="count", alias="n")]''')
s = s.replace("from ...core.semantic import SEMANTIC_TYPES\n", "")
s = s.replace("from ...query.spec import Interval, QuerySpec, Select, Sort, TimeBucket, TimePart",
              "from ...core.profile import is_temporal\n"
              "from ...query.spec import Interval, QuerySpec, Select, Sort, TimeBucket, TimePart")
p.write_text(s); print("guards added")

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# text columns that mean a timestamp but are not one
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
@pytest.fixture
def text_dates(app_ctx, run_op, tmp_path):
    """The shape of a real logon export: MM/DD/YYYY HH:MM:SS as text."""
    path = tmp_path / "logon.csv"
    with path.open("w", newline="") as fh:
        w = csv.writer(fh)
        w.writerow(["user", "date", "activity"])
        for i in range(60):
            w.writerow([f"u{i % 5}", f"{i % 12 + 1:02d}/{i % 27 + 1:02d}/2011 08:07:29",
                        ["Logon", "Logoff"][i % 2]])
    return run_op(op="import", uri=str(path), name="logon")


def test_a_text_date_column_is_not_a_time_axis(app_ctx, text_dates):
    """Meaning and storage are different questions.

    The column means a timestamp -- detection says so, correctly -- but date
    arithmetic on a VARCHAR is a type error, so nothing may treat it as a time
    axis until it is parsed.
    """
    column = app_ctx.catalog.get_profile(text_dates).column("date")
    assert column.semantic_type == "time.timestamp", "it does mean a timestamp"
    assert column.physical_type == "VARCHAR"
    assert column.role != "time", "but it cannot be used as one yet"


def test_features_on_a_text_date_explain_rather_than_fail_in_duckdb(
        app_ctx, text_dates):
    """This used to surface as 'No function matches -(VARCHAR, INTERVAL)' with a
    forty-line list of candidate operators, naming neither the column nor the fix."""
    job = run_failing(app_ctx, op="transform", plugin_id="enrich.features",
                      inputs=[{"dataset_id": text_dates}],
                      params={"features": ["count() by user over 30d"]})
    assert job.status == "failed"
    assert "normalize.timestamp" in job.error
    assert "VARCHAR, INTERVAL" not in job.error


def test_naming_the_text_column_explicitly_is_also_caught(app_ctx, text_dates):
    job = run_failing(app_ctx, op="transform", plugin_id="enrich.features",
                      inputs=[{"dataset_id": text_dates}],
                      params={"time_column": "date",
                              "features": ["count() by user over 30d"]})
    assert job.status == "failed"
    assert "not a date or timestamp" in job.error
    assert "MM/DD/YYYY" in job.error, "it says how the column does read"


def test_a_time_rollup_on_a_text_date_is_caught_too(app_ctx, text_dates):
    """The same column crashed agg.time_rollup a second earlier, in strftime."""
    job = run_failing(app_ctx, op="aggregate", plugin_id="agg.time_rollup",
                      inputs=[{"dataset_id": text_dates}],
                      params={"time_column": "date", "interval": "day"})
    assert job.status == "failed"
    assert "normalize.timestamp" in job.error


def test_parsing_it_is_the_top_suggestion(app_ctx, text_dates):
    """Nothing time-based works until this runs, so it outranks everything."""
    from dataq.services.inspect import suggest

    top = suggest(app_ctx, text_dates)[0]
    assert top.action["plugin_id"] == "normalize.timestamp"
    assert top.action["params"]["column"] == "date"
    assert top.action["params"]["format"] == "%m/%d/%Y %H:%M:%S"


def test_after_parsing_features_work(app_ctx, run_op, text_dates):
    from dataq.services.inspect import suggest

    action = suggest(app_ctx, text_dates)[0].action
    run_op(op="transform", plugin_id=action["plugin_id"],
           inputs=[{"dataset_id": text_dates}], params=action["params"])

    profile = app_ctx.catalog.get_profile(text_dates)
    assert profile.column("date_ts").role == "time"

    run_op(op="transform", plugin_id="enrich.features",
           inputs=[{"dataset_id": text_dates}],
           params={"features": ["count() by user, activity over 30d",
                                "days_since_last() by user"]})
    after = app_ctx.catalog.get_profile(text_dates)
    assert after.column("n_by_user_activity_30d") is not None
    assert after.column("days_since_last_by_user") is not None


def test_a_stale_profile_that_still_says_time_is_caught(app_ctx, text_dates):
    """Datasets imported before roles considered storage still carry role=time
    on a text column. Trusting the role reproduces the original crash on exactly
    the datasets that already exist."""
    profile = app_ctx.catalog.get_profile(text_dates)
    version = app_ctx.catalog.get_version(text_dates)
    for column in profile.columns:
        if column.name == "date":
            column.role = "time"          # as an older import would have left it
    app_ctx.catalog.set_columns(version.id, profile.columns)

    job = run_failing(app_ctx, op="transform", plugin_id="enrich.features",
                      inputs=[{"dataset_id": text_dates}],
                      params={"features": ["count() by user over 30d"]})
    assert job.status == "failed"
    assert "normalize.timestamp" in job.error

'''    def by_role(self, *roles: ColumnRole) -> list[ColumnProfile]:
        return [c for c in self.columns if c.role in roles]

    def time_columns(self) -> list[ColumnProfile]:
        """Columns usable as a time axis, which is not quite role == "time".

        The role is recorded at profiling time and can be stale -- a dataset
        imported before roles took storage into account, or a column a user
        pinned by hand -- so the physical type is checked as well. Every caller
        of by_role("time") wanted this; asking for the role alone is how a text
        column reached DuckDB as `VARCHAR - INTERVAL`.
        """
        return [c for c in self.by_role("time") if is_temporal(c.physical_type)]''')
p.write_text(s)

             "src/dataq/plugins/builtin/suggesters.py"):

    s = s.replace('by_role("time")', "time_columns()")

Do not treat a text date column as a time axis

Reported against a logon export whose date column holds '03/07/2011 08:07:29'
as VARCHAR. Detection reads it correctly as a timestamp -- 100% of values, one
unambiguous format -- and that meaning was being used as licence to do date
arithmetic on it. enrich.features emitted ORDER BY "date" RANGE BETWEEN INTERVAL
30 DAY PRECEDING, and DuckDB answered with

  No function matches the given name and argument types '-(VARCHAR, INTERVAL)'

followed by forty candidate operators, naming neither the column nor the fix.
agg.time_rollup failed the same way a second earlier, in strftime.

Meaning and storage are different questions. A column's role says what it can do
as stored, so a text date is a dimension until parsed; its semantic type still
says what it means, which is what makes the fix suggestable. The role was
previously taken from the semantic type alone, so any text column recognised as
temporal claimed a time axis it could not provide. That was true before the
format library broadened detection -- ISO-looking text hit it too -- but
recognising thirty-five formats made it easy to reach.

Three parts:

  Role reflects storage. One change, and every time-based plugin stops picking
  the column up: features, rollups, timelines, charts.

  Parsing it is now suggested, top-ranked, carrying the format already detected
  -- so the fix is one click rather than something to know about. Nothing
  suggested a normalize step before; the plugin was only reachable from the
  action menu.

  Callers ask profile.time_columns() rather than by_role("time"), which checks

  profiling time and go stale: a dataset imported before this change, or a
  column pinned by hand, still claims role=time. Without the check the original
  error returns on exactly the datasets that already exist.

Naming a text column as time_column explicitly is now an error that says the
column is VARCHAR, how it does read, and to parse it first.

Assistant2026-08-29T03:32:58.474Z

Yes — that's exactly the problem. Your date column holds 03/07/2011 08:07:29 as VARCHAR. DataQ detects that it means a timestamp (correctly — 100% of values, format %m/%d/%Y %H:%M:%S, unambiguous), and was then using that meaning as licence to do date arithmetic on text:

ORDER BY "date" RANGE BETWEEN INTERVAL 30 DAY PRECEDING
→ No function matches '-(VARCHAR, INTERVAL)'

agg.time_rollup failed the same way one second earlier, inside strftime.

Meaning and storage are different questions. A column's role should say what it can do as stored — so a text date is a dimension until parsed — while its semantic type records what it means, which is what makes the fix suggestable. Role was being taken from the semantic type alone. That predates the format work (ISO-looking text hit it too), but recognising 35 formats made it easy to reach.

Three parts to the fix:

  1. Role reflects storage. One change, and no time-based plugin picks the column up — features, rollups, timelines, charts.
  2. Parsing is now suggested, top-ranked, carrying the detected format. Nothing suggested a normalize step before; the plugin was only reachable from the action menu.
  3. Callers ask time_columns() instead of by_role("time"), checking the physical type when the question is asked. This matters for you specifically: your dataset was profiled before the fix, so it still carries role=time — without this check you'd hit the same error again.

Naming a text column explicitly now errors with the column, its type, how it does read, and what to run.

On your dataset (reload the page — your --reload server has the changes):

  • Top suggestion is now "Parse date into a real timestamp" with format: %m/%d/%Y %H:%M:%S. One click.
  • No time-based suggestion is offered until that runs, so nothing else can fail the same way.
  • I verified read-only that all 849,579 rows parse with that format — Jan 2010 to May 2011, 1,000 users. I didn't modify your data.

After parsing you'll get date_ts, and the behavioural features should work well here — 1,000 users over 16 months is a good shape for count() by user, activity over 30d and days_since_last() by user, activity.

One thing worth flagging: my Docker container was also bound to port 8000, alongside your uv run uvicorn. I've stopped it, but that overlap existed while you were testing, so if anything looked inconsistent earlier that may be why. 528 tests pass.
